SEC. 3. Form and contents of the co 'Plaint. - The complaint shall be
verified and shall state the full names of the I arties to the case. Facts showing
the capacity of a party to sue or be sued, or he authority of a party to sue or
be sued in a representative capacity, or the legal existenc~ of an organized
association of persons that is made a pa y, must be averred. In case of
juridical entities, proof of capacity to sue m st be attached to the complaint.
The complaint shall contain a concis statement of the ultimate facts,
including the evidence, constituting the cm plainant's cause(s) of action. It
shall specify the relief( s) sought, but it mar add a general prayer for such
further or other relief(s) as may be deemedjfst or equitable.
The judicial affidavits referred to in Jection 5 hereof and the relevant
evidence shall be made part of the complain .
The complaint shall include a certific tion that the ~arty commencing
the action has not filed any other action o proceeding involving the same
issue(s) before any tribunal, agency, or quas -judicial body:nor is such action
or proceeding pending before any other tr bunal, agency or quasi-judicial
body; Provided, however, that if any such a~tion is pending, the status of the
same must be stated, and should knowledge t ere of be acquired after the filing
of the complaint, the party concerned shall u dertake to notify the court within
five (5) calendar days from such knowledge.
When the party-litigant is a juridical e tity, the verification/certification
of non-forum shopping required should be eixecuted by a natural person duly
authorized by the juridical entity, through f special power of attorney or a
resolution issued by the juridical entity £ r the purpose, attached to the
complaint.
The complaint shall further be acco panied by proof of payment of
docket and other lawful fees.
Failure to comply with the forego·ng requirements shall not be
remedied by mere amendment of the complai1 t. The court, motu proprio, shall
dismiss the case without prejudice.
The submission of a false certificatio or non-compliance with any of
the undertakings therein shall constitute indi ect contempt, without prejudice
to the corresponding administrative, civil an criminal liabilities. If the acts of
a party or their counsel clearly constitut willful and· deliberate forum
shopping, the same shall be a ground for s mmary dismissal with prejudice
and shall constitute direct contempt.

SEC. 4. Prohibited pleadings and mo ions. - The following pleadings

a) Motion to dismiss, except on the£ llowing grounds:

2) That there is another action pen I ing between the same parties for
the same cause; or
3) That the cause of action is ba[;ed by a prior judgment or by
statute of limitation; .
b) Motion for reconsideration of a fin 1 order or judg;ment, except with
regard to an order of destruction is ued under Rule 20 hereof;
c) Reply, except when an actionab e document is attached in the
Answer;
d) Petition for relief from judgment;
e) Motion for extension of time to file pleadings or other written
submissions, except for the ans er for meritorious reasons and
provided that only one (1) motion for extension of time to file an
answer shall be allowed, which sh 11 not exceed thirty (30) calendar
days;
f) Motion for postponement, except i it is based on acts of God,force
majeure, or physical inability oft e witness to appear and testify.
The grounds raised for the postponement of tqe hearing due to
physical inability of the witness o appear must be justified and
substantiated. A motion for postpo ement, whether written or oral,
shall, at all times, be accompanied by the original official receipt
from the Office of the Clerk of ourt evidencing payment of the
postponement fee under Section 1 (b ), Rule 141 of the Rules of
Court, to be submitted either at the time of the filing of said motion
or not later than the next hearing d te;
g) Third-party complaint;
h) Motion to hear affirmative defense ; and
(i) Any pleading or motion which is imilar to or of like effect as any
of the foregoing.

SEC. 2. Service of summons, order and other court processes.
Summons, orders and other court processes ay be served by the sheriff, their
deputy or other proper court officer or for j stifiable reasons, by the counsel
or representative of the plaintiff or any suita le person authorized by the court
issuing the summons.
Any private person who is authorize by the court to serve summons,
orders and other court processes shall, for that purpose, be considered an
officer of the court.
If, for justifiable causes, the defendant cannot be served personally after
at least three (3) attempts on two (2) differe t dates, service may be effected:
a) By leaving copies of the sum Ions at the defendant's
residence to a person at least eight en (18) years of age and
of sufficient discretion residing th rein;
b) By leaving copies of the summon at the defend~nt's office
or regular place of business with s me competent person in
charge thereof. A competent per on includes, but is not
limited to, one who customarily eceives correspondences
for the defendant;
c) By leaving copies of the summo s, if refused entry upon
making his or her authority and pu pose known, with any of
the officers of the homeowners' association or condominium
corporation, or its chief security officer in charge of the
community or the building wher the defendant may be
found; and
d) By sending an electronic mail tot e defendant's electronic
mail address, if allowed by the co
When the defendant is a foreign pr vate juridical entity which has
transacted or is doing business in the Philip ines, as defined by law, service
may be made on its resident agent designate in accordance with law for that
purpose, or, if there be no such agent, on th government official designated
by law to that effect, or on any of its officers, agents, directors or trustees
within the Philippines.
If the foreign private juridical entity is not registered in the Philippines,
or has no resident agent but has transacted or is doing business in it, as defined
by law, such service may, with leave of court, be effected outside of the
Philippines through any of the following me ns:
a) By personal service coursed throu h the appropriate court in
the foreign country with the assist nee of the Department of
Foreign Affairs;
b) By publication once in a newspape of general circulation in
the country where the defendan may be found and by
serving a copy of the summons and the court order by
registered mail at the last known a dress of the defendant;
c) By facsimile;
d) By electronic means with the pres ribed proof of service; or
e) By such other means as the cou , in its discretion, may
direct.
Should either personal or substitu ed service fail, summons by
publication shall be allowed. In the case of juridical entities, summons by
publication shall be done by indicating then mes of the officers or their duly
authorized representative. Extraterritorial se ice of summons, as provided for
in international conventions to which the P ilippines is a party, shall also be
allowed.

SEC. 3. Answer. - Within thirty (3 9) calendar days from service of
summons, the defendant shall file his or her a swer to the complaint, including

negative defenses not pleaded in the answer shall be deemed waived, except
when the court has no jurisdiction over t e subject matter, when there is
another action pending between the same pa ies for the same cause, or when
the action is barred by a prior judgment orb the statute of limitations. Cross­
claims and compulsory counterclaims not asserted in the answer shall be
considered barred. The answer to countercla ms or cross-claims shall be filed
and served within fifteen ( 15) calendar da s from service of the answer in
which they are pleaded.

different from that prayed for; Provided, th t the court may, in its discretion,
reduce the amount of damages and attorney' fees claimed for being excessive
or otherwise unconscionable.

The parties shall set forth in their pre trial briefs, among other matters,

purpose thereof;

undisclosed information and pate s; and
(i) Such other matters as may aid in e just and speedy disposition of
the case.

SEC. 2. Procedure. -The preliminary investigation shall be conducted

a) Within ten (10) calendar days afte the filing of the complaint, the

submit his or her counter-affidavi and the affidavits of his or her
witnesses and other documentary vidence in the format required

certified as provided in paragraphs (b) and ( c) of Section 1 hereof.
The respondent shall not be allow d to file a motion to dismiss in

c) If the respondent cannot be served ith the order of the investigating
prosecutor, or if served, does nots bmit his or her counter-affidavit

d) The investigating prosecutor mays ta hearing if there are facts and

examine. They may, however, sub1 it to the investigating prosecutor

SEC. 5. Likelihood of confusion in other cases. - In detennining
whether one trademark is confusingly simila to or is a colorable imitation of
another, the court must consider the gen ral impression of the ordinary
purchaser, buying under the normally preval nt conditions in trade, and giving
the attention such purchasers usually give in buying that class of goods.
Visual, aural, connotative comparisons and overall impressions engendered
by the marks in controversy as they are en ountered in the realities of the
marketplace must be taken into account. Wh re there are both similarities and
differences in the marks, these must be eighed against one another to
determine which predominates.
In determining likelihood of confusi n between marks used on non­
identical goods or services, several factors ay be taken into account, such
as, but not limited to:
a) the strength of plaintiff's mark;
b) the degree of similarity between t e plaintiff's and the defendant's
marks;
c) the proximity of the products or se ices;
d) the likelihood that the plaintiff will bridge the gap;
e) evidence of actual confusion;
f) the defendant's good faith in adopf g the mark;
g) the quality of defendant's product r service; and/or
h) the sophistication of the buyers.
"Colorable imitation" denotes such a lose or ingenious imitation as to
be calculated to deceive ordinary persons, or such a resemblance to the
original as to deceive an ordinary purch ser giving such attention as a
purchaser usually gives, as to cause him or h r to purchase the one supposing
it to be the other.
Absolute certainty of confusion or eve actual confusion is not required
to accord protection to trademarks already re istered with the IPO.

SECTION 1. Disposal and/or destruc ion of infringing goods, related
objects, or devices; when to file motion. - A any time after the filing of the
complaint or information, a motion for the d sposal and/or destruction of the
seized infringing goods, or materials and im lements predominantly used in
the infringement, may be filed by the plain ·ff, complainant or right-holder
before the court.
There is destruction when the inti inging goods are completely
destroyed and are put beyond further us . There is disposal when the
infringing goods are effectively prohibited fr m re-entry into the channels of
commerce but may be reused for some other awful purpose.
In case the infringing goods are counte feit or pirated, the procedure for
their disposal and/or destruction shall be sum ary in nature with notice to the
defendant or the accused to his or her last kn wn address to afford him or her
the opportunity to oppose the motion. For tl is purpose, the lack of authority
of the defendant or the accused to exercise a y of the rights of the right holder
shall be a sufficient ground for the disposal and/or destruction of infringing
goods.
Counterfeit trademark goods mean goods, including packaging,
bearing without authorization a trademark w ich is identical to the trademark
validly registered in respect of such goods, r which cannot be distinguished
in its essential aspects from such a trademark and which thereby infringes the
rights of the owner of the trademark in quest on.
Pirated copyright goods means any goods which ; are copies made
without the consent of the right-holder or per on duly authorized by the right­
holder, and which are made directly or indi ectly from an article where the
making of that copy would have constituted n infringement of a copyright or
a related right.
The motion for disposal and/or destr tion shall be granted where the
violation of the intellectual property right f the owner or right-holder is
established.
In case any genuine issue is raised, sue as but not limited to, where the
infringement may involve determination of c nfusing similarity, applicability
of fair use or other limitations and exce tions, substantial equivalence,
construction of claims, and/or good faith, th court shall continue to receive
evidence of the parties during trial in suppo of their respective claims and
defenses, and the disposal and/or destructio of the goods, related objects, or

SEC. 3. Hazardous classification of i inging goods. -The infringing
goods, related objects, or devices are hazard us when they present:
a) Short-term acute hazards, such s acute tox1c1ty by ingestion,
inhalation or skin absorption, corro ivity or other skin or eye contact
hazards, or the risk of fire or explo ion;
b) Long-term environmental hazards, including chronic toxicity upon
repeated exposure, carcinogenicity which may in some cases result
from acute exposure but with a 1 ng latent period, resistance to
detoxification process such as b odegradation, the potential to
pollute underground or surface wat rs, or aesthetically objectionable
properties such as offensive odors; or
c) Unreasonable risk and/or injury t health and safety and to the
environment.
Hazardous goods, related objects, a d devices also include health
sensitive infringing goods, which are consi ered harmful as a result of sub­
standard or incorrect active phannaceutical i gredients or lack of therapeutic
benefits, which can further endanger the pub ic' s health.
Hazardous goods, related objects and devices shall only be subject to
destruction. All other infringing goods, rela ed objects and devices shall be
subject to disposal and/or destruction.

SEC. 4. Manner or method of disposa and/or destruction of infringing
goods. - The manner or method of disposal and/or destruction of infringing
goods, related objects, or devices depends o their nature and circumstances,
and whether hazardous or non-hazardous.
The proposed manner or method o disposal and/or destruction of
infringing goods must be compliant with exi ting laws and regulations.
a) The following methods of destruct·on may be allowed by the court,
depending on the nature and circm stances of the infringing goods,
related objects, or devices:
i. Crushing, shredding, and discar ing at sanitary landfills;
ii. Incineration;
iii. Encapsulation; or
iv. Other methods that do not pos any risk to the environment or
public health and safety.
Provided that open burning, or pla ing these goods in non-sanitary
and open landfills shall not be allo ed.
b) The following methods of dispos 1 may be allowed by the court,
depending on the nature and circu stances of the infringing goods,
related objects, or devices:
i. Recycling;
ii. Humanitarian donation; or
iii. Other methods that do not pos any risk to the environment or
public health and safety.
Provided that the manner of dispos 1 must effectively prevent the re­
entry of the infringing goods, rel ted objects, or devices into the
channels of commerce.

SEC. 5. Order of disposal and/or de truction of infringing goods. -
Once the court determines that the motion fur disposal and/or destruction is
meritorious, it shall issue an order of dispos~f and/or destruction of infringing
goods, related objects, or devices, including ut not limited to, sales invoices,
other documents evidencing sales, labels, si ns, prints, packages, wrappers,
receptacles, and advertisements and the lik used in the infringing act. The
order shall include the manner, method, and plan of disposal and/or
destruction, if any.
Upon issuance of the order, the ovant must comply with the
following:
a) An inventory and photographs of he infringing goods must have
been taken before the disposal and/ r destruction at the place where
the seized infringing goods are sto ed;
b) The taking of the inventory and ph tographs must be witnessed and
attested to by: ( 1) the defendant, o accused or counsel or agent, or
in their absence, an officer of t e barangay where the seized
infringing goods are stored; (2) th plaintiff, complainant or right­
holder, or his or her representative r counsel; (3) the public officer
who seized the items or a represe tative of his or her office; ( 4) a
court officer authorized by the court; and/or (5) authorized
representative of the regulatory g vernment agency involved, to
supervise the disposal and/or <lest ction of the infringing goods;
c) Representative samples of the infr· nging goods have been retained
in a number and nature as to suffic for evidentiary purposes;
d) An inventory of the representative samples has been made by the
persons enumerated under (b) abo e;
e) The court officer authorized to supervise the destruction has
submitted a report thereon, within five (5) calendar days from the
date of the disposal and/or destruc ion, to which is attached (i) the
inventory and photographs of th infringing goods and (ii) the
inventory of the representative sa les; and
f) The movant has posted a bond i an amount fixed by the court
sufficient to answer for any dam ge that the adverse party may
suffer.
Within ten (10) calendar days after th disposal and/or destruction, the
movant must file a report with the court stati g that he, she, or it has complied
with the above conditions and with the order fthe court granting the disposal
and/or destruction of the seized infringing g ods, related objects, or devices.
